passage:
A museum displayed an ancient bronze mirror. Its surface no longer reflected clearly, but the back was decorated with birds and clouds.
Students asked why a mirror needed decoration on the back.
The guide said objects can be practical and symbolic at the same time. The owner may have used it for appearance, ceremony, or status.
The mirror showed that daily objects can carry beliefs.
Modern mirrors are often plain and cheap. This one suggested that looking at oneself had once been connected to art and meaning.
The mirror no longer showed faces well, but it reflected a culture's ideas about beauty and value.
